name: Encoded Reconstruction
definition: A conceptual framework where the central artifact is an encoded record capable of reconstructing an optical field, rather than simply a three-dimensional image. The hologram stores and replays information about the light field itself, arising because the hologram stores and later replays information about the light field itself.
summary: Encoded reconstruction treats holograms as encoded records that reconstruct coherent optical wavefronts via diffraction, distinguishing them from stereoscopic or lenticular displays that do not replay the original light field.
